report:
## Conclusion: The claim is false — soursop does not cure cancer in humans

Your skepticism is well-supported by the evidence. While soursop (graviola/Annona muricata) contains bioactive compounds, especially acetogenins like annonacin, that have shown cytotoxic effects against cancer cells in laboratory (in vitro/petri dish) and some animal studies, **there is no reliable clinical evidence that it treats or cures cancer in humans**. No randomized controlled trials in cancer patients have demonstrated efficacy, and preliminary human safety/tolerability trials are only just emerging (researchsquare.com preprint).

Major cancer authorities are explicit on this: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and Cancer Research UK state that soursop's anticancer claims are not supported by clinical evidence — lab results don't reliably translate to human outcomes (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soursop). Fact-checking organizations reached the same conclusion after reviewing viral claims: PolitiFact found no human studies exist to confirm cancer-treatment efficacy (https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2022/sep/27/facebook-posts/fact-checking-claims-tree-fruit-soursop-cures-canc/), and AFP's fact-check cited the Cancer Treatment Centers of America noting soursop "has not been studied in humans," so its safety and efficacy remain unproven (https://factcheck.afp.com/scientists-say-there-insufficient-evidence-prove-mangosteen-soursop-and-coconut-water-work-natural).

There's also a safety concern: annonacin, the same compound touted for anticancer activity, is neurotoxic and has been linked to atypical Parkinsonism in populations with high Annonaceae consumption (e.g., French Caribbean studies), with toxicologists warning against supplement use (https://www.nutraingredients.com/Article/2012/05/10/Toxicology-expert-raises-alarm-over-potential-neurotoxins-in-graviola-soursop/).

**Bottom line:** Promising lab chemistry ≠ proven human cure. Relying on soursop instead of conventional treatment could be harmful and delay effective care.
